title: Clarify intake constraints, compatibility annotations and staged fallback playbook for new open-model entries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a crisp, implementation-ready set of intake requirements and an operational playbook for admitting new open-models into the catalog. This ticket consolidates ambiguous edge cases observed during recent ingests: variant naming collisions, underspecified pin semantics, runtime capability mismatches (KV cache, quantization), and unclear fallback behavior for unpinned variants. Goal: provide product + runtime engineering with acceptance criteria and rollout controls that reduce manual triage and produce deterministic behavior in hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
scope: Define a minimal metadata contract required at intake: provenance, weights checksum, expected max sequence length, recommended quantization config, and supported runtime features (KV cache, streaming, past-state retrieval).
Specify explicit pinning semantics: hard-pin, soft-pin-with-grace-period, and opt-out; include upgrade/rollback rules and who can trigger them.
Create compatibility annotation taxonomy (e.g., runtime_v1, kv_cache_compatible, low_mem_variant) and mapping to fallback model families.
Design a staged-fallback playbook for runtime mismatches that covers canary routing, automatic fallback thresholds, and operator alerting.
out_of_scope: Changes to billing/pricing or token accounting for new models.
Large-scale UI redesign of the catalog browser (tiny UX copy updates are OK).
Automated model performance benchmarking (this ticket defines what to record, not how to run heavy evals).
acceptance_criteria: A documented intake schema (JSON example) with required and optional fields and validation examples is published in the intake PRD.
Pinning semantics are spelled out in one page: definitions, state machine for transitions (hard->soft->unpinned), and role-based permissions required to change a pin.
Compatibility tags and their semantics (exact tag list) are agreed with runtime and SDK teams and added to the model-catalog schema.
Staged-fallback playbook exists and includes exact thresholds (e.g., latency > 2x baseline for 5m with 95th percentile) that trigger automatic reroute, plus runbooks for on-call.
A lightweight validation webhook prototype that rejects intake submissions missing mandatory metadata is delivered (POC script + example failures).
At least one downstream dependency (runtime) has reviewed and signed off on the compatibility tag semantics.
risks: Overly strict intake criteria could increase manual triage time and block healthy community submissions.
Vague pin semantics risk accidental forced upgrades in Dedicated/Private deployments, causing regressions for customers who pin behaviorally-critical variants.
Insufficient fallback rules could lead to silent quality regressions if an unpinned variant is swapped without proper graceful degradation.
dependencies: DES-7681: catalog intake error UX copy (validation failures)
Security-101: KMS ingestion workflow (only for flagged proprietary artifacts)
decisions: Use three pin tiers: hard-pin, soft-pin (30 day grace by default), and unpinned.
Compatibility tags will be a flat list of short tokens (no nested feature objects) to keep validation simple.
Fallback routing: prefer a same-family, lower-capacity variant before falling back to a different model family.
implementation_notes: Runtime engineering to expose a /compat-probe endpoint returning supported features and an estimated memory footprint for a given model variant.
Catalog schema to include a 'compatibility_tags' array and a 'preferred_fallbacks' array (strings of model aliases).
Intake webhook should return actionable errors (missing 'weights_checksum', missing 'max_seq_len', incompatible 'quantization_hint').
We will ship the intake validation as an opt-in guard for the first two weeks, then flip to block mode once 3rd-party submitter guidance is published.
test_plan: Unit tests for schema validation covering new required fields and error messages.
Integration test: submit a 'soft-pin' variant and exercise the pin->auto-upgrade cooldown path in a staging runtime.
Chaos test: simulate a runtime kernel failure for a family to validate automatic fallback behavior and alerting.
Manual review checklist to be used by PM/design for the first 10 community submissions after rollout.
